rename.to: [Bug] UpdateById broken due to wrong operation?

body:
So **please ignore the above**, this is the issue at hand, same entities, and the query is:
```ts
return connection
      .manager
      .updateById(ControlPlace, data.id, data)
```
However the result is:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9698639/31060872-50e95258-a6e0-11e7-9df2-efd057d0edb8.png)

You can see it tries to `select` multiple things and then **`insert`** when it should be an **`update`**.
So `updateById` selects the entity, overrides the partial entity values passed, then calls to `EntityManager`'s `save()` method, which i think doesn't make any distinction about how to save.

Found the issue, if i don't remove the id from the partial entity it breaks, had to do this:
```ts
const { id, ...control } = data
    return connection
      .manager
      .updateById(ControlPlace, id, control)
      .then(() => true)
```
@pleerock Is that normal behavior?
`update` and `updateById` will be refactored and improved soon, it must use `UpdateQueryBuilder` instead of using repository's find and save as it does now
I refactored `update` and `updateById` - now they are using update query builder - this is how they should work from the beginning. Please check latest updates in 0.1.1 once it gets released
The refactor changes are in docs?
no, changes are in internal implementation, there is no changes in public api
So i still have to extract the id of the instance before updating?, or does it accepts now the id in object?
It simply generate UPDATE query based on given `conditions`, in case of updateById based on the provided `id`.

What i meant was if i can stop the need of deleting the id of the object i'm gonna save, from this:
```ts
const { id, ...control } = data
    return connection
      .manager
      .updateById(ControlPlace, id, control)
      .then(() => true)
```
To this:
```ts
return connection
      .manager
      .updateById(ControlPlace, data.id, data)
      .then(() => true)
```
Note how in second one i don't do destructuring.
it shall work, please test it.

For some reason it says that certain relation cannot be null, which in theory should already have a value in database since is an update, seems like if i don't extract the `id` out of `data` then it doesn't take it as a partial.

it works if you only provide relations as an `id`. If you include a real entity instance, it may break _even though_ the data for the column with null constraint (in the joined entity)  is already saved. 
 `return this.updateById(foo.id, {someRelation: someRelation.id});` works. This does not work: `return this.updateById(foo.id, {someRelation});`
I was not trying any relation id, i'm talking about the entity itself, i have to extract the `id` out or it will not take it as a partial.
ok, misunderstanding. By "extract" you mean omit or remove.... Perhaps these are two different issues then (but I bet at the core it is related as it iterates through relations).

By extract i meant put it in a variable, then delete it from the object, in https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/issues/971#issuecomment-337460995 i do it by destructuring, but the same can be achieved by:
```ts
    const id = data.id
    delete data.id    //  <---- Here's where we delete

    return connection
      .manager
      .updateById(ControlPlace, id, data)
      .then(() => true)
```
